paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this one. Jehoshaphat gets a hard word from Jehu the seer, and Jehu says the wrath of the LORD is upon him for helping the wicked (2 Chronicles 19:2). But in the very same breath, Jehu says, "some good is found in you" (2 Chronicles 19:3). Then the passage says Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem, and once again he went out among the people to turn them back to the LORD (2 Chronicles 19:4).

Then look at what he tells the judges: "you are not judging for man, but for the LORD, who is with you when you render judgment" (2 Chronicles 19:6). That's the whole job right there. With the LORD there is no injustice or partiality or bribery (2 Chronicles 19:7), so whoever stands in His place has to carry that same fairness. Baker, you may never wear a robe, but you make calls all day, and somebody always ends up watching how you handle them. Same rule for you: do it like the LORD is in the room, because He is.

So when somebody corrects you, don't hide in the pantry. Take the correction, hold onto the good, and get back to work. Jehoshaphat ends with "Act resolutely; may the LORD be with the upright!" (2 Chronicles 19:11), and I want that on a cookie box. And his story isn't over, friend, so stay close.
